item.title: The principles of conduct are essentially the art of adaptation. How can one be dogmatic about a single aspect?
item.description: Exploring how to maintain the ability to be flexible and adaptable in a changing world, avoiding extreme thinking, while emphasizing the importance of the doctrine of the mean and an open mindset.
item.content:encoded:
The way of navigating life is also the art of adaptation; it cannot be rigidly fixed on one side.

Mistakes in the Last Assessment

  • My first speculative attempt, lacked consideration of the factor of project failure (or default).
  • We may need to continuously correct our judgments, because the world is changing.

Avoiding Extreme Thinking

  • Being biased toward one side means falling into extreme thinking, believing that a certain strategy or concept can apply forever, or holding an absolute view of certain things. This way of thinking ignores the complexity and diversity of reality. Navigating life and responding to change requires balance; one cannot be too aggressive, nor too conservative.
  • In economic decision-making, behavior biased toward one side may manifest as excessive reliance on a certain policy tool (such as monetary easing or fiscal stimulus), ignoring long-term side effects. Similarly, when individuals invest, if they relentlessly pursue a certain investment model, they may miss other potential opportunities.

Winning by Adapting to the Enemy

  • The world is full of uncertainty and variables, whether in politics, economics, or personal life. Facing these changes, rigidly adhering to a fixed strategy or concept will lead to mistakes, or even missed opportunities. Adaptation means adjusting one’s behavior and strategy according to environmental changes, maintaining flexibility and adaptability.
  • The “Winning by Adapting to the Enemy” mentioned in Sun Tzu’s Art of War also emphasizes the importance of responding to change. Whether facing the battlefield or various challenges in life, the ability to adapt to change often determines success or failure.

Balance and Moderation

  • The Doctrine of the Mean (Zhong Yong) emphasizes finding balance between extremes. True wisdom lies in knowing when to persist and when to change. This applies to life, career, investment, and politics. Timely adjustments not only avoid the difficulties brought by rigidity but also allow us to better seize new opportunities.
  • “Adaptation” is not blindly following change, but adjusting strategy according to the situation while maintaining core principles. This flexibility allows us to maintain direction while effectively meeting challenges.

Open Mindset

  • Responding to change also requires us to maintain an open mindset, always ready to accept new knowledge and new information. Often, success depends on whether we can timely recognize the arrival of change and take corresponding action. Those who always cling to old ideas and are unwilling to accept change are often eliminated during periods of flux.
  • In this age of information explosion, maintaining openness and critical thinking is necessary to avoid being misled and to quickly adapt to new situations and challenges.

item.title: Simple logic
item.description: A logician doesn't need to personally see or hear about the Atlantic Ocean or Niagara Falls; he can infer the possibility of their existence from a single drop of water.
item.content:encoded:
Chapter 1: Intellectual Preparation for Logic

Highlightg(yellow) - 02 Conceptualization Relates to Facts > Page 15 · Location 154 Objective existence of facts comes in two basic forms: things (entities) and events. A thing is an existing entity, such as an animal, vegetable, or mineral deposit. For example, the White House can be seen as a representative of a thing, while Lincoln being stabbed can be seen as a representative of an event.

Highlightg(yellow) - 02 Conceptualization Relates to Facts > Page 15 · Location 158 To confirm the existence of a thing, you simply need to conduct an on-site investigation.

Highlightg(yellow) - 02 Conceptualization Relates to Facts > Page 15 · Location 162 But how do we prove the authenticity of an event, such as Lincoln being stabbed?

Highlightg(yellow) - 02 Conceptualization Relates to Facts > Page 15 · Location 164 We can only rely on certain things that can serve as indirect evidence. For example, official records (police reports, death certificates, etc.), contemporary newspapers, photographs, memoirs, diaries, congressional archives, etc. All these authoritative materials from different fields can only be explained by the fact that Lincoln was stabbed.

Highlightg(yellow) - 02 Conceptualization Relates to Facts > Page 15 · Location 167 Facts can be considered objective, or they can be considered subjective. Things and events are objective; they exist in the public domain and can, in principle, be accessed by everyone. A subjective fact refers to a fact that is experienced personally by an individual or confirmed indirectly through the experience of others. For example, a headache is a subjective fact; if I experience a headache, I have firsthand evidence of its authenticity. However, if you have a headache, and not me, I can only establish my concept of a headache by indirectly hearing you describe your headache. Therefore, the confirmation of a subjective fact completely depends on the reliability of the person claiming to have the headache.

Highlightg(yellow) - 02 Conceptualization Relates to Facts > Page 16 · Location 174 Just as with indirectly verifying the authenticity of a thing, when verifying whether an event is true or false using indirect evidence, we must pay sufficient attention, because seriously reviewing the authenticity and reliability of the evidence source is the most important thing.

Highlightg(yellow) - 03 Concept Relates to Its Object > Page 16 · Location 180 A correct concept faithfully reflects the objective order of its object; conversely, an incorrect concept is a distorted expression of the objective world.

Highlightg(yellow) - 05 Concept Relates to Facts > Page 18 · Location 198 Human cognition is mainly formed by 3 parts: (1) things that exist objectively; (2) the reflection of those things in the brain; (3) the language we create for them, through which we can communicate with others. Taking a cat as an example, first there must be a cat, and only then can we establish the concept of a cat, followed by the universally recognized word “cat.” Everything originates from the objective existence of the cat; without this objective existence, there can be no concept or language about the cat.

Highlightg(yellow) - 05 Concept Relates to Facts > Page 19 · Location 206 A complex concept refers to concepts that do not correspond one-to-one with objective things. Such concepts usually have multiple sources in the objective world. For example, democracy—is it a clear and specific concept? At least subconsciously, yes, because we can link it to the objective world. But the connotation of democracy has rich sources: people, events, constitutions, legislative actions, old systems, and new systems, etc. If I want to discuss democracy with others, to avoid falling into the subjective trap and being unable to communicate with others, I must discuss things that everyone understands in reality; I must constantly involve various events in reality, and these events are the real soil of the democratic connotation.

Highlightg(yellow) - 06 Concept is Expressed in Language > Page 20 · Location 226 Language must faithfully express the original appearance of objective things, thereby giving our communication a solid factual basis. Note - 06 Concept is Expressed in Language > Page 20 · Location 227 Thus, language can also be poisoned to deceive the masses.

Highlightg(yellow) - 07 Effective Communication > Page 21 · Location 238 In logic, a statement has a specific meaning; it is a specific linguistic expression that applies only to propositions that can be judged as true or false.

Highlightg(yellow) - 07 Effective Communication > Page 21 · Location 239 Words are called the foundation of language, and propositions are the foundation of logic.

Highlightg(yellow) - 07 Effective Communication > Page 21 · Location 240 Logic itself is the study of discovering the truth and separating it from error.

Highlightg(yellow) - 07 Effective Communication > Page 21 · Location 243 Communication. If a person doesn’t even understand what they are thinking, how can they clearly express it to others?

Highlightg(yellow) - 07 Effective Communication > Page 22 · Location 246 Don’t assume that your audience will grasp the meaning you haven’t directly expressed.

Highlightg(yellow) - 07 Effective Communication > Page 22 · Location 248 Ignorance. When we are unsure, it is best to clearly state the background information; rambling is always better than being completely silent.

Highlightg(yellow) - 07 Effective Communication > Page 22 · Location 249 Say complete sentences.

Highlightg(yellow) - 07 Effective Communication > Page 22 · Location 253 Don’t treat a subjective view as an objective fact. Tai Shan is between Shandong and Shanxi—this is a proposition based on objective facts; it is either true or false. But if I say, “Tai Shan is beautiful,” this proposition blends subjective and objective factors. In this case, we absolutely cannot arbitrarily judge the truth or falsity of a subjective proposition, as we just did. The truth or falsity of an objective proposition is undisputed, but that of a subjective proposition is not. If I want a certain subjective proposition to be accepted by everyone, I must argue for it.

Highlightg(yellow) - 07 Effective Communication > Page 23 · Location 257 Avoid double negation.

Highlightg(yellow) - 07 Effective Communication > Page 23 · Location 261 Choose appropriate language based on the object.

Highlightg(yellow) - 08 Avoiding Vague and Ambiguous Language > Page 24 · Location 276 One way to avoid ambiguity is to ensure that the words you use reflect your intended meaning as specifically as possible, so that the reader or listener does not have to strain to guess what you mean.

Highlightg(yellow) - 08 Avoiding Vague and Ambiguous Language > Page 24 · Location 279 Words like “love,” “democracy,” “fairness,” “kindness,” and “evil” inherently have unclear meanings. This is not just because they lack a fixed reference, but also because their meanings are too broad. Therefore, even if two people use the same word (e.g., “love”), their meanings can be vastly different, or even contradictory. This is why, when using such words, they must be accurately understood. Before you try to convince someone that something is unfair, you must tell them how you define unfairness.

Highlightg(yellow) - 09 Avoiding Evasive Language > Page 25 · Location 289 Try to speak plainly and directly to reduce the possibility of the listener misunderstanding what you mean. But this does not mean you should be unrestrained; a person should be able to perfectly combine conciseness with elegance.

Highlightg(yellow) - 10 Truth > Page 26 · Location 297 The purpose of all logical reasoning and all argumentation is singular: to find the truth of a certain thing.

Highlightg(yellow) - 10 Truth > Page 26 · Location 300 Truth comes in two basic forms: ontological truth and logical truth. Among these, ontological truth is more fundamental. Ontological truth refers to truths concerning existence. If a thing is determined to be an ontological truth, and it truly is, then it must exist somewhere. A lamp on a table is an ontological truth because it truly is there, not an illusion. The opposite of ontological truth is a false illusion.

Highlightg(yellow) - 10 Truth > Page 26 · Location 306 Definition of a proposition: A linguistic expression that can be judged as true or false. To affirm a proposition is to judge it as true, and vice versa.

Highlightg(yellow) - 10 Truth > Page 27 · Location 311 Confirming the truth means achieving the unification of the subjective and the objective.

Highlightg(yellow) - 10 Truth > Page 27 · Location 314 The basis for determining the truth or falsity of a proposition is the real situation, and logical truth is built upon the foundation of ontological truth.

Highlightg(yellow) - 10 Truth > Page 28 · Location 325 Language logic should be based on factual logic.

Chapter 2: Basic Principles of Logic

Highlightg(yellow) - 01 Basic Principles > Page 31 · Location 332 Logic is the analysis of thought.

Highlightg(yellow) - 01 Basic Principles > Page 31 · Location 340 Law of Identity Statement: A thing can only be itself. This explains the rich and colorful reality, which is composed of countless individuals, and each individual is unique. A thing can only be itself, and not something else. An apple is an apple; it is not an orange, nor a banana or a pear.

Highlightg(yellow) - 01 Basic Principles > Page 32 · Location 343 Law of Excluded Middle Statement: For any judgment about a thing under certain conditions, there must be a clear “is” or “is not”; there is no intermediate state. This explains that a thing either exists or does not exist, with no middle ground. A lamp on a table—this statement is either true or false, with no other possibility.

Highlightg(yellow) - 01 Basic Principles > Page 32 · Location 353 Law of Sufficient Reason Statement: Everything has a sufficient reason for its existence. This principle can also be called the causal principle. It embodies the content that the existence of all things in the universe has a sufficient basis.

Highlightg(yellow) - 01 Basic Principles > Page 33 · Location 362 Law of Contradiction Statement: At the same time, a thing cannot be both this way and not this way in the same respect. This principle can be seen as an extension of the Law of Identity: if X is X (Law of Identity), then at the same time, it cannot be non-X (Law of Contradiction). The qualifier “in the same respect” refers to the mode of existence. At the same time, a thing can be both and not at different respects, which is not a contradiction.

Highlightg(yellow) - 02 Gray Area and Man-made Gray Area > Page 36 · Location 400 Negation can only be confirmed when the positive is known.

Highlightg(yellow) - 03 Everything Has Its Origin > Page 37 · Location 411 There must be a fundamental similarity between every cause and its effect. This means that a cause must lead to the observed effect and leave its specific imprint on the result; every effect, to a certain extent, reflects the characteristics of its origin.

Highlightg(yellow) - 04 Don’t Give Up the Search for Causes > Page 37 · Location 421 The search for causes should not be abandoned halfway. Causes are often a series. For example, A is the cause of B occurring, and the occurrence of B leads to C. We can represent their relationship graphically: A → B → C. Let’s assume C represents a difficult problem in the event that needs to be remedied. We find that C is caused by B. Following the correct method for solving affairs—the principle of finding its cause—we decide to focus on B. This logical approach is commendable, but it hasn’t gone far enough. B is indeed the direct cause leading to C, but it is not the root cause. The source of the causal chain is A, so A is the fundamental cause of problem C.

Highlightg(yellow) - 05 Distinguishing Causes > Page 39 · Location 439 Let’s analyze the “Four Causes” using a birdcage as an example. Its efficient cause is Friede, who manufactured it; its material cause is pine wood, nails, screws, and paint; its formal cause is the specific shape of the birdcage (which distinguishes it from things like filing cabinets or window lattices); and its final cause is providing a place for small birds to perch.

Highlightg(yellow) - 05 Distinguishing Causes > Page 40 · Location 456 The best tool in the hands of an unqualified person will not yield the best results. Bookmark - 05 Distinguishing Causes > Page 40 · Location 457

Highlightg(yellow) - 06 Defining Terms > Page 40 · Location 459 The most effective way to avoid semantic confusion and ambiguity in a logical argument is to define terms. When we say “define terms,” we are actually defining the objective thing that the term represents. The process of definition is the process of giving it a precise “position” based on how it relates to other things (the thing to be defined).

Highlightg(yellow) - 06 Defining Terms > Page 40 · Location 464 The logical process of defining terms is divided into two steps: First, placing the term to be defined into the closest category; second, determining its unique characteristics that differentiate it from other things in the same category.

Highlightg(yellow) - 06 Defining Terms > Page 41 · Location 466 The classic definition of a human is “a rational animal.” In this definition, “animal” is the closest category, the category most closely related to humanity. Why?

Highlightg(yellow) - 06 Defining Terms > Page 41 · Location 473 In Aristotle’s definition of man, “rationality” is the characteristic that distinguishes man from other animals. A special characteristic is called a genus (or specific property), and it determines a specific category and distinguishes it from other categories.

Highlightg(yellow) - 06 Defining Terms > Page 41 · Location 477 Justice: Step 1: “Justice is a social virtue…” Step 2: “…through justice, every member of society receives everything due to them.”

Highlightg(yellow) - 06 Defining Terms > Page 42 · Location 484 Fear: Step 1: “Fear is an emotion…” Step 2: “…that prompts us to avoid perceived danger.”

Highlightg(yellow) - 06 Defining Terms > Page 42 · Location 489 If we want to define “mobile phone,” Step 1 can be quite simple: the category is “communication equipment”; then, we must emphasize several special distinguishing characteristics to differentiate it from other communication equipment in the world.

Highlightg(yellow) - 06 Defining Terms > Page 42 · Location 490 The unique value of a logical definition lies in its ability to reveal the essence of the defined thing.

Highlightg(yellow) - 07 Declarative Proposition > Page 43 · Location 499 The most effective arguments have conclusions that are declarative propositions, clearly and explicitly telling us what the truth of a thing is.

Highlightg(yellow) - 07 Declarative Proposition > Page 44 · Location 504 A proposition may be declarative in form, but the content it expresses may still be incorrect. A person might say, “The Chicago baseball team is the best baseball team.” This is a declarative proposition, but it only tells us the speaker’s firm belief. It describes a subjective fact because it is merely the speaker’s opinion, and does not reflect any objective situation.

Highlightg(yellow) - 08 Universal Proposition > Page 45 · Location 528 Logic is the technology that allows one to believe in the truth.

Chapter 3: Argumentation: The Language of Logic

Highlightg(yellow) - 01 Establishing an Argument > Page 48 · Location 534 A logician does not need to have seen or heard the Atlantic Ocean or Niagara Falls; they can infer the possibility of their existence from a single drop of water.

Highlightg(yellow) - 01 Establishing an Argument > Page 49 · Location 547 The most effective argument always tries to reach the simplest and clearest conclusion.

Highlightg(yellow) - 01 Establishing an Argument > Page 49 · Location 557 The premise is the foundation of the argument; a correct argument relies on correct premises. Therefore, the first step of a correct argument is to confirm the correctness of the premises.

Highlightg(yellow) - 03 From Particular to Universal > Page 50 · Location 568 The process of arguing from universal to particular ensures the necessity of the conclusion, but the reverse is not guaranteed. For partially valid conclusions, we cannot definitively say that they hold true for the whole. In some examples, the process of arguing from particular to universal leads to clearly erroneous conclusions. “Some women are mothers” is an absolutely correct proposition, but this premise does not support the conclusion “All women are mothers.”

Highlightg(yellow) - 03 From Particular to Universal > Page 51 · Location 577 Just because certain characteristics are suitable for a part of the whole, it is not necessarily true that these characteristics are suitable for the whole. This is a clear fallacy. However, people often cannot avoid this fallacy, so when facing such situations, one should be extra careful. Hasty generalization is a kind of human nature, although it is not a good thing.

Highlightg(yellow) - 04 Assertion > Page 51 · Location 582 Assertion is the process of linking the concept (predicate) to the subject.

Highlightg(yellow) - 04 Assertion > Page 52 · Location 583 If assertion is the process of gathering and pairing concepts, then testing the correctness of the assertion lies in whether the gathered concepts actually fit together in reality.

Highlightg(yellow) - 06 Comparison > Page 54 · Location 623 When we compare two things, we find that they are either completely similar, completely different, or partially similar.

Highlightg(yellow) - 07 Comparison and Argumentation > Page 57 · Location 657 Argument Summary: A has characteristics R, S, T, U, V, W, X, and Y. B has characteristics R, S, T, U, V, W, X, and Y. A has characteristic Z. Therefore, B also has characteristic Z. Analyzing this conclusion is not necessary, but it is highly probable. Based on the fact that two things possess many common characteristics, when one of those things has another characteristic, it is highly likely that the other thing also possesses it. Analogical argumentation is only applicable when we cannot directly prove that B has characteristic Z; of course, it can also be when B has not yet occurred, so it cannot be analyzed.

Highlightg(yellow) - 08 Correct Argumentation > Page 58 · Location 669 To make an argument correct and powerful, we must pay attention to its facts (content) and its form (structure).

Highlightg(yellow) - 08 Correct Argumentation > Page 58 · Location 679 Conjunctive Argumentation: The symbolic representation of conjunctive argumentation is: A $\cdot$ B. Here, A and B both represent a complete proposition. item.description:
All Animals Are Equal, But Some Animals Are More Equal Than Others

The absurd slogans and constantly revised rules are Orwell’s primary tools for exposing how totalitarian regimes manipulate, deceive, and suppress the masses through language. These slogans appear simple and easily understandable, aligning with the interests of the animals, but in reality, they are cleverly twisted and utilized by the rulers (the pigs). All Animals Are Equal, But Some Animals Are More Equal Than Others

The absurd slogans and constantly revised rules are Orwell’s primary tools for exposing how totalitarian regimes manipulate, deceive, and suppress the masses through language. These slogans appear simple and easily understandable, aligning with the interests of the animals, but in reality, they are cleverly twisted and utilized by the rulers (the pigs). Ultimately, they betray the original intent of the revolution, plunging the other animals back into a state of oppression and exploitation.

Four Legs Good, Two Legs Bad

Absurdity: This was the animals’ original slogan, used to distinguish themselves (representing the proletariat and revolutionaries) from humans (representing the exploiters and rulers). This slogan emphasizes that all four-legged animals (as well as the two wings of birds) are superior to two-legged creatures (i.e., humans). However, as the pigs’ power gradually increased, they eventually learned to walk upright, and the slogan was subsequently changed (see the next point). Function: This simple and memorable slogan helped the animals unite against humans, but simultaneously, it overly simplified complex reality, failing to recognize the intricate hierarchies and evolving class struggles among the animals themselves.

Four Legs Good, Two Legs Better

Absurdity: As the pigs slowly imitated humans and gained more privileges after the revolution, they quietly changed the slogan to “Four Legs Good, Two Legs Better,” betraying the original revolutionary intent. This change reveals the process of power corruption, showing that the pigs gradually became indistinguishable from the enemy they initially overthrew (humans). Function: This new slogan symbolizes the pigs’ complete domination of the farm and their betrayal of the other animals. By changing the language and rules, they confuse the other animals about the facts, gradually accepting the pigs’ new rule.

All Animals Are Equal, But Some Animals Are More Equal Than Others

Absurdity: This is one of the most famous absurd slogans from Animal Farm. It originally came from the first of the Seven Commandments of Animalism, “All Animals Are Equal,” but as the pigs’ power grew, they modified it to “Some Animals Are More Equal Than Others.” This statement is clearly self-contradictory, because equality itself implies no difference, yet the phrase “more equal” reveals the inherent unfairness of reality. Function: This slogan reflects how the rulers (the pigs) established a new class system by masquerading as equality. Through this linguistic manipulation, they make the other animals accept their subordinate status, while the pigs enjoy privileges.

Comrade Napoleon Is Always Right

Absurdity: Napoleon is the leader among the pigs, gradually becoming a dictator. This slogan implies that any action taken by Napoleon is flawless, absolutely correct, and beyond question. It is a typical totalitarian strategy that asserts the infallibility of the leader, thereby suppressing any dissent or criticism. Function: This slogan eliminates the space for opposition and questioning by promoting the absolute authority of the leader, causing the other animals to blindly follow him, regardless of how absurd or selfish his decisions may be.

Work Harder, Comrade Napoleon Is Right

Absurdity: This slogan is often repeated by a horse named “Boxer.” He believes that problems will eventually be solved through working harder, and that Napoleon is always correct. This blind loyalty and self-sacrifice reflect the trust of the common laborers (symbolizing the working class) in the ruling class, even when the ruling class is constantly exploiting them. Function: By promoting the values of labor and sacrifice, the rulers use this slogan to make the other animals work tirelessly without questioning the distribution of power or the injustice of the system.

Don’t Believe What You See, Believe What You Hear

Absurdity: This phrase is used by Napoleon’s propagandist, “Squealer,” to tell the animals not to trust the facts they see with their own eyes, especially when those facts contradict the party’s propaganda. This is similar to the concept of “doublethink” described by Orwell in 1984, which requires people to ignore reality and accept the false explanation provided by the rulers. Function: This slogan aims to distort the animals’ perception of reality, preventing them from questioning the pigs’ actions or decisions. This is a typical method used by totalitarian regimes to maintain their power by manipulating information and propaganda.

item.title: Always Say Less Than Necessary
item.description: Parents teach us how to speak in a single year. And we must use a lifetime to learn how to be silent. When you try to use language to move others, the more you speak, the more mediocre you appear, and the more mistakes you make. This is roughly the meaning of “language carries Zen insight”: the less you speak, the greater the unknown, and humans are naturally fearful of the unknown.

item.title: One must not show one's brilliance too much, as it will provoke jealousy and fear.
item.description:
Everyone is like Wu Dalang; when running a shop, they dislike having staff taller than themselves. Like Liu Bang, there are too few people who are more capable than oneself and can be effectively managed, so you won’t encounter them. The vast majority of leaders are Wu Dalang, so when you display your abilities, you might cause them to become wary of you.

Always make those above you feel comfortably superior. In your desire to please and impress them, do not go too far in displaying your talents or you might accomplish the opposite – inspire fear and insecurity. Make your master appear more brilliant than they are and you will attain the heights of power.

item.title: A philosophy of life: Don't look at how this person treats you; look at how she treats the other people around her.
item.description: This article explores the relationship between personal behavioral habits and one's intrinsic values and beliefs, pointing out that how a person treats others often reflects how they will also treat you.
item.content:encoded: A person’s behavioral habits are often formed over a long period, and they reflect their intrinsic values and beliefs. If a person treats the people around them with friendliness, respect, and kindness, then they are also more likely to be friendly to you. Conversely, if a person treats the people around them with indifference, selfishness, and rudeness, then they are also more likely to be indifferent, selfish, and rude to you.

item.title: Tolerate the fool, understand the fool, harvest the fool.
item.description: This article explores the complex relationship between influencing higher-level interests and changing lower-tier perceptions, pointing out that the two are actually intrinsically linked, because lower-level perceptions form the foundation of higher-level interests.
item.content:encoded: Do not disturb the interests of the upper stratum, nor should you disturb the mindset of the lower stratum. Disturbing the interests of the upper stratum is akin to taking his life, while disturbing the beliefs of the lower stratum is like digging up his ancestral grave, and the beliefs of the lower stratum are precisely the source of the upper stratum’s interests.

You must learn when to step away temporarily to elevate your value through absence.

  1. Humans are habitually curious creatures, always hoping to deduce something consistent from the actions of others.   1. The best way is to mingle among the crowd, find allies, and blend in. The crowd is the best shield.
  2. Isolation cuts off your valuable sources of information, making you highly visible and an easy target for attack.

Power Law 19: Know Who You Are Dealing With—Never Target the Wrong Person

  1. If you trick certain people once with a scheme or tactic, they will seek revenge for life. These people are wolves in sheep’s clothing. You must choose your opponent or victim extremely carefully; never offend or deceive the wrong target.

Power Law 20: Don’t Depend on Anyone

  1. Only fools rush to choose which side to stand on.

  1. The tactic is to make your opponent feel that they are very smart—not just smart, but smarter than you. Once they believe this, they will never suspect you have hidden motives.

  1. Don’t give them the satisfaction of fighting and defeating you—surrender first.

  1. Find rich deposits and dig deep; the harvest will be much greater than shallow, scattered digging. Depth and intensity must surpass width and breadth.

Power Law 24: Play the Perfect Courtier

  1. The perfect courtier is always capable and adaptable. They master the art of indirect advancement, flattering and serving the powerful, while simultaneously demonstrating their power in the most indirect, subtle, and elegant way.

  1. Always pay attention to your image and become the master of your own image; do not let others define it for you.
  2. Do not readily accept the role society imposes on you. Reshape a new identity that is both eye-catching and not tiresome to the audience.

Power Law 26: Maintain Personal Integrity and Purity

  1. You must maintain your spotless image. When necessary, you can use others as scapegoats or pawns to conceal your unspeakable actions.

  1. First, your words should be deliberately vague, but they must contain words of commitment, emphasizing fervor over rationality and clear thinking.   3. Enhance your charisma with striking images and radiant features, making others feel that your presence is extraordinary.

  1. Anger and loss of control are counterproductive strategically; therefore, you must always remain calm and objective. If you can provoke the enemy while remaining calm yourself, you have gained a decisive advantage.

item.description:
1. Fallacy of Assertion: In this fallacy, the assertion does not provide sufficient evidence or support, but merely claims a fact as a declaration. For example: “Everyone knows I am the smartest person.”

  2. Fallacy of Causation: This fallacy lies in incorrectly assuming a causal relationship between two events. For example: “I ate strawberry ice cream, so it caused the weather to get cold.” This fallacy ignores other factors that might influence the weather.
item.content:encoded:
1. Fallacy of Assertion: In this fallacy, the assertion does not provide sufficient evidence or support, but merely claims a fact as a declaration. For example: “Everyone knows I am the smartest person.”

  2. Fallacy of Causation: This fallacy lies in incorrectly assuming a causal relationship between two events. For example: “I ate strawberry ice cream, so it caused the weather to get cold.” This fallacy ignores other factors that might influence the weather.

  3. Ad Hominem Fallacy: In this fallacy, the arguer is attacked, rather than the argument itself being rationally debated. For example: “This plan is unwise because it was proposed by a foolish person.”

  4. Appeal to Emotion: In this fallacy, one attempts to persuade people to accept a certain argument by exciting their emotions rather than through logic and evidence. For example: “Support this policy, and let’s create a better future together.”

  5. Appeal to Invalid Authority: In this fallacy, one attempts to use an invalid or irrelevant authority to support an argument. For example: “Celebrity X likes this product, so it must be good.”

  6. Hasty Generalization: This fallacy involves drawing overly broad conclusions based on limited evidence or samples. For example: “I saw two people who didn’t like this movie, so everyone won’t like it.”

  7. False Analogy: In this fallacy, an argument is supported by making an inappropriate or unsuitable comparison. For example: “Feeding vegetables to children is like feeding them to pets; it’s all for their own good.”

  8. Chain of Fallacy: In this fallacy, a false premise leads to a series of false conclusions. For example: “If we don’t change the education system, our economy will collapse; if the economy collapses, our society will collapse; therefore, we must change the education system.” There is no reasonable logical connection between the premise and the conclusion here.

  9. Metaphysical Fallacy: In this fallacy, an incorrect conclusion is drawn from the meaning of language or words. For example: “Money is a form of energy, so if I have enough money, I can control everything.”

  10. Appeal to Ignorance: In this fallacy, it is assumed that because something cannot be proven true or false, it must be either true or false. For example: “No one can prove the existence of aliens, so aliens must exist.”

  11. False Dilemma (or Either/Or Fallacy): In this fallacy, the issue is simplified to only two choices, ignoring other possible options. For example: “You either support Party A or support Party B; there is no other choice.”

  12. False Continuum (or Continuum Fallacy): In this fallacy, it is incorrectly assumed that there is an infinite continuity between two extremes, ignoring possible intermediate ground. For example: “If you don’t agree with my view 100%, then you are against my view.”

  13. Fallacy of Composition and Fallacy of Division: The fallacy of composition involves applying the characteristics of an individual to an entire group, or applying the characteristics of a group to each individual. For example: “The football team of this school is strong, so every student in this school is an excellent athlete.”

  14. Gambler’s Fallacy: In this fallacy, it is incorrectly assumed that there is a necessary balance between random events, believing that previous results will influence future results. For example: “Five heads have appeared in a row when tossing a coin, so the next one must be tails.”

  15. Fallacy of Past Belief: In this fallacy, it is assumed that past beliefs or views must be correct. For example: “Our ancestors believed the Earth was flat, so the Earth must be flat.”

  16. Fallacy of Assuming the Conclusion: In this fallacy, the conclusion is used as a premise to support one’s own argument. For example: “This book is the Bible of truth because everything it says is true.”

  17. Fallacy of Self-Contradiction (or Contradictory Premises): In this fallacy, the premises of the argument contradict each other, leading to an invalid conclusion. For example: “I will never lie; right now, I am lying.”

  18. Fallacy of Loaded Question: In this fallacy, the question itself is misleading, making it difficult for the respondent to answer without falling into a trap. For example: “When will you stop hitting your wife?”

item.content:encoded:
Hello everyone, and welcome to the final episode of Deeply Loving Wealth (or Deeply Loving Finance). I’m JS Jing Shu. As for what the future blog or other content will be, I’ll save that for the next episode—that is, the first episode of the new podcast. Since this is the last one, I’m just going to go a little crazy. I’m giving up on being Lin Blogger’s face, or whatever. I’m just done with it.

I want to say something that I’ve always wanted to say: Scholar Cat is toxic. So today, I don’t want to play around with being non-judgmental or making benevolent assumptions about these mind-body-spirit contexts. Because if I hold that idea, of course, it’s not wrong, but my words just won’t make sense, and this sentence will never be fully articulated.

So, today is a very subjective, very emotional episode. This is my background. If you want to say that what he talks about definitely has good aspects, then I agree, of course, but if I keep going back and forth like this, I just can’t produce this episode today. So, just think of it as me going crazy, or maybe even chasing traffic, or maybe you just want to eat some gossip, listen to some chatter—that’s fine. In this episode, I’ll talk about some phenomena I’ve observed in Scholar Cat’s community. But more importantly, I hope you listen to this episode with the following questions in mind. First, what constitutes a toxic thought? How do we define which idea is toxic and which is relatively healthy? Second, why are cults or organizations with extreme and bold ideas so attractive? Third, why does the community easily develop a pathological attachment? And how do we prevent it? Fourth, what are the historical, social, and economic contexts of the mind-body-spirit teachings we are currently exposed to? Have you ever thought about this? And fifth, how do we engage in independent thinking? Since this episode primarily aims to encourage independent thinking, you shouldn’t believe everything I say; you must make your own judgment.

I even feel that if you, hey, truly want to think independently, you’re curious, and you go, but you still spend 999 [currency unit] to join Scholar Mom’s community, or you spend the current 9999, or whatever to buy her course, it doesn’t matter. It means you are truly making a judgment based on your own personal experience. If you have money, you can do that. Right, let me give you another background detail. I also thought that since I am discussing a larger topic today—the entire mind-body-spirit industry—we will talk about the chain of capitalism and consumerism later. Do I need to single out Scholar Cat? And is it better to just talk about the industry to appear more rational, objective, and neutral? But I thought about it, if I just talk about it that way, first, it will be rather dry. Second, my thoughts on this industry are indeed derived from my experience in Scholar Cat’s community. And there are many things that I actually want to express, but due to friendship, or because I want to be a spiritual blogger, I haven’t expressed them.

So I also guess that many of his friends in the community have similar thoughts. So I dare to express some of my very subjective ideas, hoping that through this method, I can make the topic I want to discuss today more concrete—it’s a process of non-self-censorship. Okay, so today we have several chapters. I’ll list them: Chapter 1 is titled, “Why I Say This Community is Toxic,” which is my personal experience in the Scholar Cat Planet Knowledge Circle community. First, let me talk about the historical background. I met Scholar Cat around 2018 through the introduction of Teacher Zhang Xiaoyu. At first, we clicked really well, and soon became good friends. During that time, we basically communicated daily on WeChat, sharing a common hobby, and reading some very… well, mind-body-spirit related books. At that time, I felt it was a mutually supportive relationship, because, well, Scholar Cat’s community wasn’t like it is today, where everything seems to have an answer. We would ask each other questions, and I would ask him questions. It was in that state, and we discussed a book called The Guide to Living in the Present.

At that time, Scholar Cat was a very precious friend to me. He supported me during a very difficult period in my life, and we went out and played together. But around 2019, we started drifting apart because I noticed he began to move towards the path of “paying to win” (氪金)—spending a lot of money, buying luxury goods, or going to high-end hotels. In short, high-end consumption. At the same time, he also started focusing on the Zero Limit path.

For those who don’t know, I’ll explain Zero Limit later, but generally, this Zero Limit method isn’t my cup of tea. I didn’t criticize it much at the time; I just felt, “Yeah, I don’t like it. It’s too simple and too brainless.” I didn’t like this school of thought. More importantly, as I slowly interacted with him, I started to feel a strange sensation: we were no longer in a relationship of equal friends.

Because it seemed like every time we chatted, whether sitting down to eat or online, he seemed to know everything, understand everything, and could constantly output information, output his thoughts, his understanding, and try to inspire you, guide you, and help you open up your perspective, loosen your thinking. What is this? If this were a teacher and a student, if both of you agreed to enter such a hierarchical relationship, then of course, you can constantly listen to a teacher explain things to you. But if it’s friends, I think the foundation of friendship is that both are human—that both are, first and foremost, human. Which means both have flaws, both have weaknesses, and both have doubts. I think this is a basic commonality of being human. But chatting with Scholar Cat, the more and more I felt like he was a teacher, an old soul. He seemed to have very few doubts or vulnerabilities. I rarely heard him talk about any of his doubts or uncertainties. Of course, in his community, the nuances are even more subtle; he talks about his, say, his relationship experiences, which we will discuss later. But overall, he is someone who is not very… well, not showing weakness, not having any confusion. Slowly, I started to find it boring.

But in 2022, I saw that his official account had written a lot about paying to win, about how many people, under his guidance, had had very stimulating experiences through aggressive means. Yet, the overall style of the articles was very calm. It allowed you to feel, even amidst those very stimulating events, that “this makes sense,” and also feel that kind of cosmic great love. It felt like these two things combined created a huge contrast, which was also very interesting. So, when I frequently read his stuff, I have complex feelings: “Ugh, isn’t this nonsense?” But then I think, “Ah, it’s humorous, it makes sense,” and then I think, “Hmm, it’s going off the beaten path,” and then I think, “This person is very unique,” and then I feel a bit of envy, jealousy, and hatred. Sometimes I think, “Should I learn more about this?” And sometimes I feel, “Hmm, something might be wrong.” In short, I am constantly pulled back and forth between these complex emotions and thoughts.

Then, at a certain stage, I started thinking, why don’t I delve deeply into what he is talking about? On one hand, I wanted to reconnect with my old friend; on the other hand, I felt that perhaps the many things he talks about—things I don’t know, for example, I don’t have as much experience in finance as him—might be a new input, a new cognition for me, and truly help open something up for me. So, last year, I joined his community to get a close look at this person and his ideas. My background is in law and anthropology. As a legal professional, I have a principle I strongly adhere to.

In my knowledge system, if I don’t understand him, I should best presume that he is benevolent, presume that what he has is valuable, and then rationally view it, criticizing it only when necessary. So I still believe in this principle of presumption of innocence. As an anthropologist, I have curiosity, and I think the most important quality of an anthropologist is the willingness to immerse oneself in a culture. During the immersion process, of course, you temporarily set aside your critical thinking. For example, imagine you go to a primitive tribe. If you are constantly thinking, “What is this tribe all about?” you might find it difficult to truly understand this tribe from within, what it is like to be a member of this tribe. Of course, you can never truly become a member of that tribe; you still have your own nurtured background, your social background plays a huge role behind the scenes. But you try to put aside your preconceptions—the knowledge and insights you have gained previously—and allow yourself to truly be changed and permeated by that person or that community’s culture, and then look at yourself after being permeated.

It’s equivalent to the anthropologist studying an object using their own body, using their very genuine experience. So, of course, my entry into this community isn’t that high-brow; it’s not like I’m conducting an anthropological study. It’s just that I have this background. So I am very willing to truly assume that my previous ideas might have some limitations, some blind spots, and I want to experience, think, and act like a member of Scholar Cat’s community.

So, this experiment lasted for quite a long time—I think six or seven months. I kept myself in this mode of thinking and acting to see what kind of content was in Scholar Cat’s community. It actually covers three very important topics that everyone cares about. I heard people jokingly say that if you cover these three topics, any product or content you make will be bought, will go viral, and will make money. That’s “Get Rich, Get Lay, Don’t Die”—meaning get rich, and get laid (sex/love/intimacy), and then health.

Scholar Cat’s community covers these three topics: health, romance/marriage, and wealth. We can elaborate on these later. And these three topics are all underpinned by a grander cosmic view, a philosophy, or you could say a grand worldview, which is the Zero Limit cleansing method. So, you see, this structure is very deceptive. It places itself between very grand, very enlightened spiritual teachings and very bold, even gambler-like practices. The wealth, health, and romance—these all have a bit of that gambler-like quality, like they are trying to achieve something big with something small, or achieve cosmic-level rewards in a very clever way. That’s the general mindset. It bombards your nervous system every day with different chemical elements.

What are these chemical elements mainly? For example, adrenaline, which makes you very excited and anxious. Dopamine, which makes you addicted. But occasionally, there are very truthful or very soul-resonating feelings, like endorphins and oxytocin, that are at work. Do you feel like sometimes you are anxious, sometimes you are calm? This back-and-forth bombardment actually makes you very addicted. And this addiction constantly leads back to love and peace, finally to cleansing. But we still have to buy, buy, buy; we still have to eat, eat, eat; we still have to do something stimulating. This state of addiction is probably why many of us, including myself, and many of the community members want to check his Planet. So, next, let’s look at these topics one by one, and how they relate to this underlying worldview.

So, next I will divide it into several sections: one about Zero Limit, the second about paying to win, the third about 369 (the health diet method), and then about love and the overall community atmosphere. I will explain them in detail. First, although I have already made the judgment that this place is toxic, you can measure it yourself after hearing the details. So, those who are non-judgmental, you can leave now; you don’t have to listen to this episode. For those who are non-judgmental, you can enter this community. I should add that, of course, we practice Nonviolent Communication, and in some way, mind-body-spirit teachings force us to notice our habitual judgments, our complaints, our aggressive tendencies—like the habits of online trolls. But if you use it to review your own views and thoughts, and if it makes your naturally sharp, pointed thinking process dull, then…

You know, if you throw a “non-judgmental,” “cannot-be-judged,” or “don’t be too black-and-white” umbrella over things, who knows? When you throw this big umbrella, your sharp thoughts are immediately blurred, like a fog, and everything becomes like paste. I prefer to become very subjective and very extreme rather than dilute my views with that umbrella, with that paste-like fog.

First, Zero Limit. What kind of teaching is Zero Limit? It says that first, you must be 100% responsible for yourself. Everything you see is also your responsibility, even if someone else experiences pain—it is still within your own consciousness. So it must be cleansed by yourself. Pain is a replay of memory. So, for example, if you suffer some injustice in society, or if you, say, are robbed, or assaulted, it is still a memory of victimization playing back within yourself. So what you need to do is cleanse that memory. Everything else that goes wrong and causes pain is like that. You just need to take full responsibility for everything, even if someone hits you, you are responsible for it. Then you must delete, you must cleanse those memories. Similarly, others are your projections. So, this community likes to say NPC, which stands for Non-Player Characters. Just like when you play a game, only you are the real player. The other people who appear, even though they seem to be talking to you, their conversations are programmed. So, within this Zero Limit mindset, others are NPCs. Heh. How is this self-consistent? Are all of us NPCs? The general idea is that we are all NPCs. In my world, only I am real; I am 100% responsible for myself, and everyone else is my projection, an NPC.

So, even if others say something that hits me, or they hurt me in some way—for example, many people in the community were scammed—the person who was scammed is still an NPC. Ultimately, we are responsible for it ourselves, for returning it to ourselves, for cleansing the greed or the tendency to pick up small gains, or the fear within ourselves. How do you cleanse it? Zero Limit tells us that in some primitive tribe in Hawaii, they use this method to cleanse by constantly saying four phrases: Sorry, Please forgive, Thank you, I love you.

Or these four phrases are called PONO. There are many Zero Limit related products now. You see, this is truly an industry. You can buy, say, a notebook where you check off 1,000 times a day for cleansing. You constantly recite this, and it is also a form of meditation. Don’t you think so? Because whatever you do, even if you recite it 1,000 times, you can achieve a form of cleansing or enter a meditative state. You recite anything, it actually prevents your brain from thinking about other things temporarily. And you do it 1,000 times a day, or some people don’t do 1,000 times, but they constantly recite it in their minds. When you think of it, in your daily social life, when someone says something, you constantly think, “Sorry, please forgive, thank you, I love you.” Scholar Mom herself says that during her interactions with others, when she hears someone speak, she constantly silently recites these four phrases. So, this is a very highly self-consistent thought system. It is a closed system. It first tells you that everything is extremely, extremely your responsibility.

And other things, you don’t need to worry about them. You cleanse yourself, and the outside world will change. After you cleanse yourself, you will have… wealth comes, but he is also very smart. He says this cleansing is not just to make you rich or help you find an ideal partner, because if that’s the case, you still have a thought. So all thoughts must be cleansed. It looks very wise and profound.

Because when you cleanse everything to that absolute state of zero, it is indeed a grand and wide state that many practitioners or meditators pursue or experience. So it seems to be one level higher than other manifestation laws, because other manifestations say, “If you do these things, you will get these.” But the higher point of Zero Limit is that you must cleanse the thought that you will get those things. Even if you get them, you must cleanse that thought that the thing is good.

It is actually a bit like Vipassana. Vipassana ultimately says that you must zero out both the good and the bad. It actually has these ideas. So, this is any practice that might have some benefits. When it is used to the extreme, or when you use it brainlessly, it will produce some distorted things. For example, when using Zero Limit, or especially in Scholar Cat’s practice, if you have any doubts, you must cleanse that doubt. So, it is equivalent to it being unbeatable and never wrong. And you must constantly reinforce yourself and form a closed loop. Otherwise, you will keep doubting yourself. If you doubt, you cannot cleanse, unless you cleanse your own doubt. Do you understand this logic? So, if you have any dissatisfaction with the cleansing method, any doubt, any confusion, you…

And he adds a supplement: cleansing, or many current mind-body-spirit schools, have a bit of a contemptuous way of thinking. They feel that our society has always been like a pendulum. You see, our mainstream society or science, this modern society, it emphasizes rationality and downplays the body, the intuition, and the spirituality. Then, in the spiritual world, you swing to another extreme, where you constantly emphasize the body and intuition, and the signals of the universe, and you must submit to them. You must be brainless. He even thinks “brainless” is a good word. You must let go of your rational judgment, don’t analyze so much, don’t debate. Debate is also the biggest vice that prevents enlightenment. Don’t criticize, don’t think, don’t have those opposing forces. Look at the words I just said. If you change one to a softer one, without opposition, letting go of your thinking, letting go of your analysis, then it becomes a very reasonable, very soul-soothing meditation phrase. So, you see, hahaha, the same sentence, said with different tones, has different effects.

In short, in Zero Limit, don’t over-doubt, don’t over-think. Just chant like a fool. In Scholar Cat’s community, “chanting like a fool” is a good phrase. It means that even if you don’t understand what Zero Limit is at first, you constantly have doubts, but it doesn’t matter. You just repeat it like a fool. You repeat it to a certain degree, and you are truly brainwashed. You are truly changed, internalized, and permeated by his love, by those cosmic truths. So, you just keep repeating it.

For myself, I truly try to believe in this system, especially when I have many doubts. I think, “How come? I almost said, ‘Oh, I’m so unhappy, I’m so easily negative, complaining,’ because I questioned too much, because I like to dig into this matter, to figure it out to the root, and to research the origin of Zero Limit.”

For example, in India, not just in some primitive tribe in Hawaii, I really wanted to know how the primitive tribes did it. But the people who really practice Zero Limit don’t care how the primitive tribes did it; they just culturally appropriate and plunder it, and use it in a very fragmented way. But my personality is not like that; I cannot chant like a fool. So I struggled for several months. I tried to truly do it, but now I can finally announce that I can’t, haha. If this process helped me in any way, it helped me understand myself more clearly, and more clearly know how my path should be. For example, I truly don’t believe that negative thoughts are just cleansed when you chant them. When you keep chanting, it’s cleansed. This idea is too naive. Think about it: if your consciousness is a screen, a stage, and you constantly fill it with 1,000 Zero Limit cleansing mantras, after a while, of course, the negative thoughts will disappear, and you will feel how amazing it is—they really disappeared. But does that mean they are truly gone? For me, I still believe in the Jungian/Freudian idea: you actually have an unconscious. When your negative thoughts and negative emotions disappear right now, it doesn’t mean they are gone; it just means you have violently suppressed them 10,000 times, they naturally run deeper into the unconscious. You suppress them 10,000 times, they are naturally gone.

This kind of Zero Limit cleansing, I think it definitely has short-term benefits. It can temporarily bring you back to peace, and it gives you a feeling that if you are particularly obsessed with “this is good” or “that is bad,” it can help you loosen that thought. But for someone who has been on the path of self-cognition and self-growth for a long time, I think it is not helpful, or even detrimental. What is the biggest detriment? It makes you grow a spiritual ego. You might almost believe that you are that kind of person. But actually, if we look at it from the perspective of IFS (Internal Family Systems) in psychology, you have grown a huge spiritual EGO. This part completely dominates your daytime, your main consciousness. What is that part? It’s constantly chanting, “Sorry, please forgive, thank you, I love you.”

It constantly feels that everything in this world is the best arrangement, and when looking at anything, it can only be viewed from a spiritual perspective, a cosmic arrangement perspective, and everything is being manifested by you, being sent to you by the universe, and all misfortune is a gift, and so on. Slowly, you brainwash yourself, and that ego takes over your entire life.

Look, why do we say that spiritualism has great power and influence? It’s because whether you eat a meal, poop, or interact with colleagues and friends, whatever you do, it is in your background. I previously ran a whole course called “Little Master.” This is how people in the mind-body-spirit field are easily misled by this “Little Master.” You develop this Little Master who guides your life every day, and you think, “I’ve improved, I’ve achieved results!” There is nothing more absurd and contrary to the path than this, which is further away from the truth of knowing yourself. We certainly cannot fully know the truth, but at least we must approach it. But this rational ego makes it increasingly difficult for you to approach the truth of yourself.

In short, look, the Zero Limit cosmic love, combined with the fact that you only focus on yourself, and are highly narcissistic and indifferent, it is a distorted hybrid. On one hand, it has profound, possibly ancient spiritual practices, like I mentioned, similar to Vipassana. On the other hand, it makes you truly become a good… well, I cleanse everything myself, and the suffering of others—that is because they haven’t cleansed themselves; they are still playing their own game. They want to play that game of suffering. Look, with this method, you can completely isolate yourself. You can even beautify it and call it “The Great Dao is Ruthless,” “Heaven’s Dao is Ruthless.” I just cannot empathize or sympathize much with those who are suffering.

So, look, once you are permeated by this worldview, you really won’t look at the news because you can’t accept it. After you look at it, you cannot accept that it is not a dream or a game. If you slightly allow that spiritual ego to retreat a little, you will find that this world is not the way your spiritual view says it is. At least from the perspective of the other part, it is not like this. You don’t allow yourself to see it that way, because you must truly allow yourself to soften a little. If you allow yourself to soften a little, you cannot look at the news. So, you see, to a certain extent, these mind-body-spirit things are building a spiritual wall, a dike, for us. It is actually sealing it off. You have to build a bubble for yourself, build a shell, build a very protective one, only then can you survive in your highly self-consistent little bubble. This is also something I couldn’t do for a long time. I would look at the news, and I would feel inconsistent. Or I would constantly use this dominant Zero Limit method to convince myself when looking at the news. The feeling of pain… Yes, yes, now you know that a few months before I slowly started coming out of this toxic thing, I found that every time I looked at the news, whether positive or negative, I truly felt more things, which made me feel that I was truly alive. Of course, this is a later point. Previously, my good friend, Qing, who is a news reporter, also had a critique of the news—he said the news is another kind of bubble—but this is more detail, which we can discuss later. But at least I am willing to truly look at current affairs news, or look at some more documentary materials. And even if all the documentaries have their own biases, I won’t easily jump to the conclusion before watching, saying, “We must view this through a spiritual lens.” I no longer have that lens. Okay, this is the first one: Zero Limit. The second, let’s talk about the trend of paying to win in Scholar Cat’s community. Paying to win, simply put, is the belief that the more you spend, the more you have. The more you spend, the easier you spend, it means you are in a state of abundance regarding money. You believe it is infinitely abundant, it is constantly flowing. You spend it, and it flows back. You don’t have to hold onto it so tightly. On the contrary, if you feel that money is scarce, that it’s not enough, and you don’t dare to spend, the more you don’t dare to spend, the more you are in that frequency of scarcity, and the less money you have.

Another idea is the encouraging approach: don’t look at the price of the goods, don’t look at the price; just buy what moves your heart. What does “just buy what moves your heart” mean? It means you see a handbag, a watch, a hotel that moves your heart, and you don’t care how much it costs; you just buy it, and that’s it. Because the universe will support you in living in that frequency of moving heart. Plus, with the backing of the Zero Limit we talked about earlier.

Of course, what thoughts do we need to cleanse? For example, “I don’t have money,” or “I am afraid of losing money,” or “I feel ashamed about spending money,” or “I feel ashamed about becoming a millionaire.” In short, all beliefs related to money must be cleansed. Especially those beliefs that make you poor, you must constantly chant the mantra: “Sorry, please forgive, thank you, I love you.” Okay, so this is the theory of paying to win. Scholar Cat himself is constantly practicing it; he almost never says that he doesn’t go out to high-end restaurants and high-end hotels every day, and he frequently goes shopping and buys many expensive things.

Besides spending money, paying to win in this community is also manifested by many people taking on debt. Is debt a bad thing, or even a good thing in this community? For example, I know many community members; some of them are indebted by 1 million, some by 500,000, some by 100,000 or 200,000. And what do they do? What is the logic? If you truly believe that money is an energy, that it is flowing, then debt is also a flow. You don’t care whether the number is positive or negative. You can experience, say, being indebted by 1 million, and that is a huge perspective, a huge scale. And you can enjoy how luxurious, how unique, the things are that you usually can’t enjoy—those things open up your perspective. You win. In the future, you will definitely earn back this 1 million. Even if you don’t earn it back, it doesn’t matter. Look, this is the power of Zero Limit. It doesn’t say that the goal of your debt is necessarily to become a millionaire, because it doesn’t even encourage you beforehand. At least on the surface, it doesn’t encourage you to earn more money, because the thought of earning more money must also be cleansed.

But look, even though he says that, why do so many people embrace this idea? It will give you a framework, and you will know that when you hear a new thing, you can connect it with other knowledge. You won’t think, “Oh, this is amazing, it seems to be the truth.” You…

Our world has been around for thousands of years, so many philosophers, so many thinkers, step by step laid the foundation, and developed a little new idea based on the ideas of predecessors. How can you be so amazing that you can completely break away from their ideas and create your own new idea, and discover a cosmic truth? It’s not that simple. If you learn a little philosophy, history, and politics, you know these things are accumulated bit by bit. And besides reading these books, I also suggest everyone read useless books, because people in the personal growth circle love to read various technical, various… anyway, methods for self-improvement, it’s also an addiction. So you should read poetry, read sci-fi, read martial arts, read things that don’t improve yourself, to balance your information sources. Besides reading more books, the second point I want to talk about is colliding with people, debating more. Look, people in the mind-body-spirit field avoid debating because there is a kind of spiritual ego that says, “We are one,” “We are all unified,” “The world is harmonious.” Whatever you have, I can merge it into you, whatever you have, we can tolerate all emotions, all thoughts. So, in the end, this is a kind of enlightenment, a paste. It blurs things, and you feel that if you don’t think deeply, you feel that things can be compatible.

P—many things, you believe it can be compatible even if in the end, but the premise is that there is a huge rupture and many incompatibilities and dislikes. Only after debating, after fighting to the death, will they merge. This is Hegel’s idea of thesis and antithesis. First, you rupture, then you repair. Don’t be afraid of this rupture. People in the mind-body-spirit field are so afraid of rupture. How much are there? About the trauma of conflict. You pretend that you are especially harmonious, and you say, “I don’t mind, I, I don’t care if others criticize me, I don’t want to argue with people,” how noble you are, how elegant. I always feel that this is a band-aid. So, debating means solving it. It means you must first express it, like I am doing now, I am going crazy, I said a bunch of things. It doesn’t matter, don’t censor too much, just express it first. Of course, someone will disagree, and you can’t make everyone like you, and it’s okay if you are wrong, it’s okay if you are biased. Many of the things I said today are intentionally biased. I can’t make everything round, and I don’t want to do that. I just want to bring out my biased things, and welcome correction from me, welcome self-correction. I will slowly merge. Look at what I said today, I almost hate Scholar Cat. Of course, he has things that benefit me, this is not a justified hatred. I might slowly merge into it. Ugh, I don’t feel as angry as today. It might happen, but I can’t say, because it will happen. All these words I said today, I must say them. So you will find a very interesting thing: independent thinking is not achieved alone. Please remember this point: independent thinking is not achieved alone; it must be through collision. You must express it, and debate with people, discuss, explore, impact, friction, rupture, and then merge again. This is true independent thinking.

And this is the trap of our current mind-body-spirit generation: forcing every person back into their own small world, not caring about politics, not caring about others. Once your own logic is self-consistent, you don’t want to listen to other people’s logic, and you constantly self-cleanse, constantly self-reflect. You cannot recognize other aspects of society, you cannot view the world from the political perspective of other societies. It is a process that makes us lose the ability to think independently.

And the third point is that we must maintain a soft heart. What does soft mean? If you are narcissistic, you lock up your heart. Whether it is due to inferiority or arrogance, your soft part is locked up. So, to be soft means you will feel pain. Seeing a forest fire, seeing someone suffer, seeing a house collapse, you will feel pain. You just let that pain linger a little. Because I used to have a habit: when I see such painful news, I want to turn it off, I don’t want it to affect my mood for a long time. To a certain extent, this is the case. You cannot let it carry you away, and then you are depressed for the whole day, two days, three days. I think the method is to constantly learn how to adjust your nervous system so that it can coexist with this suffering, this pain in society, instead of just putting an ‘X’ on these pains and turning them off. Look, this is a very different path. When you close your heart, your heart becomes hard. That is your most precious thing; don’t defend yourself. So, one day, if you don’t feel pain when seeing these things, it’s not because you achieved enlightenment, or you achieved it, or you ascended to heaven. It’s because you cultivated it, you cultivated yourself to death.

If we say that very few people achieve enlightenment, this world is soft, and at the same time, it has a very strong place, and it can be regulated, but its hand is soft. It doesn’t lock itself up. When it sees separation and suffering, it still sheds tears. It’s not like, “I already know it is the universe’s operation principle, so these things won’t move me,” and I just cultivate myself, I cleanse myself.

Oh, this is also what they like to say: if there is war in the world, famine, strong suffering, hardship, then it must be that my unconscious, my inner self also has these things. And I must cleanse the desire or the memory and habit of fighting with others, fighting the war with others, then the world will be better. Pfft, damn it, I’m so angry. Right? So don’t cultivate it like this. If you cultivate it like this, you cultivate yourself to death. Ugh, this is also… I am not anxious, but my eunuch is anxious. Why be anxious? Look, if I say this pile of things, Scholar Cat will just smile calmly, he definitely won’t be angry, because anger is what a cultivated person would do. He would definitely say, “You are overthinking,” or look, you are like this suffering, he wouldn’t say anything, he would silently go back to cleanse it. And he would also make me cleanse it, if he still talks to me.

Anyway, today is my rambling self-talk, which is the end of my Deeply Loving Wealth. Why am I ending this blog? Because I feel that the atmosphere presented in the entire blog is a kind of… although I initially said I was an atheist, but slowly I have started to solidify my thinking. So, I think this podcast cannot continue. If I continue, I will still be talking about God, the universe, and so on. I think I’ve talked enough about those things, and those things definitely have some help. The many meditation audios before, many people feel they are helpful. If they are helpful, then they are helpful.

See you in a different Bubble.

Hahaha, hope that Bubble has more ventilation. Right? Because I cannot escape all bubbles. I just hope that whatever I do in the future is not so closed. By the way, if you don’t know, I have actually closed the Octopus Awakening community, so you can no longer join it. But Circle China is still there. The hope is to break away from some of the drawbacks of the mind-body-spirit circle, but it might still accommodate some, because I have learned so much over the years, so I am still thinking about what form and what content it will be. So during this brewing period, I hope you can generously give me some financial support.

Recently, there hasn’t been too many cases, because I feel that in this period of change, I haven’t met new people. I hope to leave more white space for my own time, so that new ideas can emerge more freely. Just like I said earlier, the most luxurious and biggest privilege is time. And I am willing to give myself so much luxurious privilege. So if you are willing to support my process of independent thinking, I hope you can support me on Ai Fa Dian or directly find my donation QR code on the WeChat official account, and you can support me after any article.

Speaking of this, I think my current view of wealth is not just how many luxury goods you can buy, or how much liquidity you have today.
